what_happened: On 2026-11-06 the person running Athena lifted the scope-guard pause on the stale-job retry line for the second time and retried it by hand, outside any job. A third job that had passed its checks went stale that night, because main moved. Each stale loss cost about $2 to $7. The latest attempt failed only on where one decision entry was placed. The person running Athena judged that one more resumed try, at about $4, costs less than the losses it stops. No acceptance criteria, findings or checks are listed for this event.
cause: The scope guard counts spend per line and never asks why an attempt did not land. A passed job that went stale because main moved, or one that failed only on a small placement fix, looks the same as progress-less spend. Athena cannot carry verified work onto a new base, so staleness shows up as a failed attempt. Nothing records the pause reason, whether a kept candidate exists, or the expected cost of a resume. So the guard has no rule for "checks passed, only the base or a small placement was wrong", and a person must judge the cost-benefit and lift the pause each time. This is the third such lift today.
prevention: Make the scope guard classify each attempt's outcome before it counts spend. When all checks and verification passed and the attempt stopped only for staleness, an environment reason, or a small fix, the spend is not counted as progress-less. The guard would then keep a candidate for resume and show the resume's expected cost. The pause would record its reason and lift itself, or ask for a decision, when the cost of a resume is below the recent loss. Pair this with a path that rebases verified work onto the new base, so staleness stops costing a full attempt.
proposed_request: Change the scope guard so it classifies why an attempt did not land before counting its spend on a line. Outcome: an attempt whose checks and verification passed, and which ended only because main moved (stale base), for an environment reason, or for a small placement or wording fix, is not counted as progress-less spend and does not pause the line. When a pause does happen, record its reason, whether a kept candidate exists, and the expected resume cost, and show them in the status output. Acceptance: (1) a test with a passed-then-stale attempt shows the line is not paused and the retry resumes the kept candidate; (2) a test with repeated attempts that failed checks still pauses the line; (3) the pause record names its reason and the resume cost estimate; (4) replaying the three stale-job lifts from 2026-11-06 against the new rule shows none would have paused. Reconcile any docs/decisions.md entry that describes the scope guard.
